title: Minority Businesses: Hong Kong deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Local caution: A city with high costs: test one small offer before you sign a lease.
Money moves fast by bank transfer and fast-payment apps; customers expect instant confirmation.
Add tax and duty explicitly; never bury them in a price. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Some activities need an extra licence (food, health, money, education centres). List yours before you take a first order. Check with a local expert.
Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit well; many one-person firms need flexible support.
Break-even units = fixed monthly cost divided by contribution per unit; round up.
Keep a registered address and a named contact; a shared-office address is common for a first year.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Protect customer and owner data; share only what a form requires, and keep a copy of what you sent.
Break-even units = fixed monthly cost divided by contribution per unit; round up.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?
Start with one need in your own community that you know well and can serve better than others.

questions.q: In "Find and serve customers Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Compare three models: sole trader, shared co-operative, or supplier to larger firms.
Show proof beyond identity: a sample, a reference and a clear result for a buyer.
A dense, trade-led city. Space is costly, so online and shared-space models fit well.
Dates: first test, first order, first review.
